summary: Burundi’s migration authority (CGM) says its single-entry visa (visa d’entrée simple) lets a foreign citizen enter and stay in Burundi for one month only, and is obtained online, at Melchior Ndadaye International Airport or at embassies. No Burundian official source we could read states which nationalities need a visa; the UK and Canadian governments, among the governments shown by passport on this page, say their citizens do. The CGM lists a free EAC entry visa for citizens of East African Community member states, valid for 1 to 6 months.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Burundi?
faq.answer: No Burundian official source we could read states which nationalities need a visa for Burundi; the UK government says British visitors must have one, and Canada’s travel advice says a tourist visa is required. Burundi’s migration authority (CGM) says the single-entry visa is obtained online, at Melchior Ndadaye International Airport or at embassies. The CGM lists a free EAC entry visa for citizens of East African Community member states; the EAC names its Partner States as the DR Congo, Somalia, Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Uganda and Tanzania.

faq.question: Which passports get a free EAC visa?
faq.answer: The migration authority (CGM) lists a free “EAC entry visa” for citizens of East African Community member states, valid for 1 to 6 months; the EAC names its Partner States as the DR Congo, Somalia, Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Uganda and Tanzania.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Burundi?
faq.answer: Burundi’s migration authority (CGM) says the single-entry visa is obtained online, at Melchior Ndadaye International Airport or at embassies, and that the transit visa (USD 40, valid for three days) is granted at any point of entry. The UK government says visas are issued on arrival in Burundi, and that all travellers without a valid settlement visa or permanent residence must complete the Airport entry visa or Transit visa application before arriving.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Burundi?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says that to enter Burundi you must have a certificate proving you have had a yellow fever vaccination, and Australia’s Smartraveller says you’ll need a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Burundi.

faq.question: Is Burundi safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to parts of Burundi, including the Mugina, Cibitoke, Bukinyayana, Bubanza and Mpanda communes and the RN6 and RN10 roads through the Kibira National Park, and says armed group activity and conflict along the border with the DR Congo has increased. The Government of Canada advises avoiding non-essential travel to Burundi.

countryFacts.payments.text: Burundi is largely a cash-based society. Take US dollars dated post-2006. Most businesses will not accept or exchange older currency and US dollars with small tears will also be rejected. You can usually exchange euros and British pounds.
Outside Bujumbura credit and debit cards are rarely accepted, and there are not many ATMs. Do not rely on cash withdrawals. You can often use mobile money in tourist hotels.
There’s a shortage of foreign exchange currencies in Burundi and an unofficial FX exchange rate exists. The unofficial rate can be substantially different from the official exchange rate.

countryFacts.safety.text: FCDO advises against all travel to Mugina, Cibitoke, Bukinyayana, Bubanza and Mpanda communes due to the risk of the presence of a rebel group in the Kibira National Park and possible armed incursions from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

FCDO advises against all travel on the main RN6 and RN10 roads running west from Kayanza through the Kibira National Park towards Cibitoke, due to the risk of the presence of a rebel group and possible armed incursions from DRC.
Avoid travelling by road outside Bujumbura after dark, because of the security situation and road safety concerns.
Avoid non-essential travel to Burundi, due to the ongoing conflict in neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo, violent crime, and the risk of political violence.

tips.cash-usd.text: Burundi is largely a cash-based society. Take US dollars dated post-2006. Most businesses will not accept or exchange older currency and US dollars with small tears will also be rejected. You can usually exchange euros and British pounds.
Outside Bujumbura credit and debit cards are rarely accepted, and there are not many ATMs. Do not rely on cash withdrawals. You can often use mobile money in tourist hotels.

tips.photography.text: Photography of sensitive installations is prohibited. This includes: ports military sites government buildings people in uniform Always ask permission before photographing official buildings or individuals.

tips.security-advisories.text: FCDO advises against all travel to Mugina, Cibitoke, Bukinyayana, Bubanza and Mpanda communes due to the risk of the presence of a rebel group in the Kibira National Park and possible armed incursions from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

FCDO advises against all travel on the main RN6 and RN10 roads running west from Kayanza through the Kibira National Park towards Cibitoke, due to the risk of the presence of a rebel group and possible armed incursions from DRC.
Armed group activity and conflict along the border between Burundi and DRC has increased.
